1.sahih_international: A supplicant asked for a punishment bound to happen
1.pickthall: A questioner questioned concerning the doom about to fall
1.yusuf_ali: A questioner asked about a Penalty to befall-
1.shakir: One demanding, demanded the chastisement which must befall
1.muhammad_sarwar: Someone has (needlessly) demanded to experience the torment (of God),
1.mohsin_khan: A questioner asked concerning a torment about to befall
1.arberry: A questioner asked of a chastisement about to fall

2.sahih_international: To the disbelievers; of it there is no preventer.
2.pickthall: Upon the disbelievers, which none can repel,
2.yusuf_ali: The Unbelievers, the which there is none to ward off,-
2.shakir: The unbelievers-- there is none to avert it--
2.muhammad_sarwar: which will inevitably seize the disbelievers.
2.mohsin_khan: Upon the disbelievers, which none can avert,
2.arberry: for the unbelievers, which none may avert,

3.sahih_international: [It is] from Allah, owner of the ways of ascent.
3.pickthall: From Allah, Lord of the Ascending Stairways
3.yusuf_ali: (A Penalty) from Allah, Lord of the Ways of Ascent.
3.shakir: From Allah, the Lord of the ways of Ascent.
3.muhammad_sarwar: No one can defend him against God, the Lord of the exalted positions.
3.mohsin_khan: From Allah, the Lord of the ways of ascent.
3.arberry: from God, the Lord of the Stairways.

4.sahih_international: The angels and the Spirit will ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years.
4.pickthall: (Whereby) the angels and the Spirit ascend unto Him in a Day whereof the span is fifty thousand years.
4.yusuf_ali: The angels and the spirit ascend unto him in a Day the measure whereof is (as) fifty thousand years:
4.shakir: To Him ascend the angels and the Spirit in a day the measure of which is fifty thousand years.
4.muhammad_sarwar: On that Day (of Judgment), long as fifty thousand years, the angels and the Spirit will ascend to Him.
4.mohsin_khan: The angels and the Ruh [Jibrael (Gabriel)] ascend to Him in a Day the measure whereof is fifty thousand years,
4.arberry: To Him the angels and the Spirit mount up, in a day whereof the measure is fifty thousand years.

5.sahih_international: So be patient with gracious patience.
5.pickthall: But be patient (O Muhammad) with a patience fair to see.
5.yusuf_ali: Therefore do thou hold Patience,- a Patience of beautiful (contentment).
5.shakir: Therefore endure with a goodly patience.
5.mohsin_khan: So be patient (O Muhammad SAW), with a good patience.
5.arberry: So be thou patient with a sweet patience;

6.pickthall: Lo! they behold it afar off
6.yusuf_ali: They see the (Day) indeed as a far-off (event):
6.shakir: Surely they think it to be far off,
6.muhammad_sarwar: They think that it (the Day of Judgment) is far away.
6.mohsin_khan: Verily! They see it (the torment) afar off,
6.arberry: behold, they see it as if far off;

7.muhammad_sarwar: but We see it to be very near.
7.arberry: but We see it is nigh.

8.sahih_international: On the Day the sky will be like murky oil,
8.pickthall: The day when the sky will become as molten copper,
8.yusuf_ali: The Day that the sky will be like molten brass,
8.shakir: On the day when the heaven shall be as molten copper
8.muhammad_sarwar: On the day when the heavens become like molten metal.
8.mohsin_khan: The Day that the sky will be like the boiling filth of oil, (or molten copper or silver or lead, etc.).
8.arberry: Upon the day when heaven shall be as molten copper

9.sahih_international: And the mountains will be like wool,
9.pickthall: And the hills become as flakes of wool,
9.yusuf_ali: And the mountains will be like wool,
9.shakir: And the mountains shall be as tufts of wool
9.muhammad_sarwar: and the mountains become like wool,
9.mohsin_khan: And the mountains will be like flakes of wool,
9.arberry: and the mountains shall be as plucked wool-tufts,

10.sahih_international: And no friend will ask [anything of] a friend,
10.pickthall: And no familiar friend will ask a question of his friend
10.yusuf_ali: And no friend will ask after a friend,
10.shakir: And friend shall not ask of friend
10.muhammad_sarwar: even intimate friends will not inquire about their friends,
10.mohsin_khan: And no friend will ask of a friend,
10.arberry: no loyal friend shall question loyal friend,

11.sahih_international: They will be shown each other. The criminal will wish that he could be ransomed from the punishment of that Day by his children
11.pickthall: Though they will be given sight of them. The guilty man will long to be able to ransom himself from the punishment of that day at the price of his children
11.yusuf_ali: Though they will be put in sight of each other,- the sinner's desire will be: Would that he could redeem himself from the Penalty of that Day by (sacrificing) his children,
11.shakir: (Though) they shall be made to see each other. The guilty one would fain redeem himself from the chastisement of that day by (sacrificing) his children,
11.muhammad_sarwar: though they may see each other. A sinner will wish that he could save himself from the torment of that day by sacrificing his children,
11.mohsin_khan: Though they shall be made to see one another [(i.e. on the Day of Resurrection), there will be none but see his father, children and relatives, but he will neither speak to them nor will ask them for any help)], - the Mujrim, (criminal, sinner, disbeliever, etc.) would desire to ransom himself from the punishment of that Day by his children.
11.arberry: as they are given sight of them. The sinner will wish that he might ransom himself from the chastisement of that day even by his sons,

12.sahih_international: And his wife and his brother
12.pickthall: And his spouse and his brother
12.shakir: And his wife and his brother
12.mohsin_khan: And his wife and his brother,

13.sahih_international: And his nearest kindred who shelter him
13.pickthall: And his kin that harboured him
13.shakir: And the nearest of his kinsfolk who gave him shelter,
13.muhammad_sarwar: his kinsmen who gave him refuge (from hardship)
13.mohsin_khan: And his kindred who sheltered him,

14.sahih_international: And whoever is on earth entirely [so] then it could save him.
14.pickthall: And all that are in the earth, if then it might deliver him.
14.yusuf_ali: And all, all that is on earth,- so it could deliver him:
14.shakir: And all those that are in the earth, (wishing) then (that) this might deliver him.
14.mohsin_khan: And all that are in the earth, so that it might save him.
14.arberry: and whosoever is in the earth, all together, so that then it might deliver him.

15.sahih_international: No! Indeed, it is the Flame [of Hell],
15.pickthall: But nay! for lo! it is the fire of hell
15.yusuf_ali: By no means! for it would be the Fire of Hell!-
15.shakir: By no means! Surely it is a flaming fire
15.muhammad_sarwar: By no means! For the raging flames of the fire
15.mohsin_khan: By no means! Verily, it will be the Fire of Hell!
15.arberry: Nay, verily it is a furnace

16.yusuf_ali: Plucking out (his being) right to the skull!-
16.mohsin_khan: Taking away (burning completely) the head skin!

17.sahih_international: It invites he who turned his back [on truth] and went away [from obedience]
17.pickthall: It calleth him who turned and fled (from truth),
17.yusuf_ali: Inviting (all) such as turn their backs and turn away their faces (from the Right).
17.shakir: It shall claim him who turned and fled (from truth),
17.muhammad_sarwar: and drag into it anyone who has turned away (from obeying God),
17.mohsin_khan: Calling: "[O Kafir (O disbeliever in Allah, His angels, His Book, His Messengers, Day of Resurrection and in Al-Qadar (Divine Preordainments), O Mushrik (O polytheist, disbeliever in the Oneness of Allah)] (all) such as turn their backs and turn away their faces (from Faith) [picking and swallowing them up from that great gathering of mankind (on the Day of Resurrection) just as a bird picks up a food-grain from the earth with its beak and swallows it up] [Tafsir Al-Qurtubi, Vol. 18, Page 289]
17.arberry: calling him who drew back and turned away,

18.yusuf_ali: And collect (wealth) and hide it (from use)!
18.shakir: And amasses (wealth) then shuts it up.
18.muhammad_sarwar: and who accumulated wealth without spending it for a good purpose.
18.mohsin_khan: And collect (wealth) and hide it (from spending it in the Cause of Allah).

19.yusuf_ali: Truly man was created very impatient;-
19.shakir: Surely man is created of a hasty temperament
19.mohsin_khan: Verily, man (disbeliever) was created very impatient;

20.shakir: Being greatly grieved when evil afflicts him
20.muhammad_sarwar: When they are afflicted, they complain,

21.sahih_international: And when good touches him, withholding [of it],
21.pickthall: And, when good befalleth him, grudging;
21.yusuf_ali: And niggardly when good reaches him;-
21.shakir: And niggardly when good befalls him
21.muhammad_sarwar: but when they are fortunate, they become niggardly
21.mohsin_khan: And niggardly when good touches him;

22.yusuf_ali: Not so those devoted to Prayer;-

23.sahih_international: Those who are constant in their prayer
23.pickthall: Who are constant at their worship
23.yusuf_ali: Those who remain steadfast to their prayer;
23.shakir: Those who are constant at their prayer
23.mohsin_khan: Those who remain constant in their Salat (prayers);

24.sahih_international: And those within whose wealth is a known right
24.pickthall: And in whose wealth there is a right acknowledged
24.yusuf_ali: And those in whose wealth is a recognised right.
24.shakir: And those in whose wealth there is a fixed portion.
24.muhammad_sarwar: They are those who assign a certain share of their property
24.mohsin_khan: And those in whose wealth there is a known right,
24.arberry: those in whose wealth is a right known

25.sahih_international: For the petitioner and the deprived -
25.pickthall: For the beggar and the destitute;
25.yusuf_ali: For the (needy) who asks and him who is prevented (for some reason from asking);
25.shakir: For him who begs and for him who is denied (good)
25.muhammad_sarwar: for the needy and the deprived,
25.mohsin_khan: For the beggar who asks, and for the unlucky who has lost his property and wealth, (and his means of living has been straitened);
25.arberry: for the beggar and the outcast,

26.sahih_international: And those who believe in the Day of Recompense
26.pickthall: And those who believe in the Day of Judgment,
26.yusuf_ali: And those who hold to the truth of the Day of Judgment;
26.shakir: And those who accept the truth of the judgment day
26.muhammad_sarwar: who acknowledge the Day of Judgment,
26.mohsin_khan: And those who believe in the Day of Recompense,
26.arberry: who confirm the Day of Doom

27.sahih_international: And those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord -
27.pickthall: And those who are fearful of their Lord's doom -
27.yusuf_ali: And those who fear the displeasure of their Lord,-
27.shakir: And those who are fearful of the chastisement of their Lord--
27.muhammad_sarwar: who are afraid of the torment of their Lord,
27.mohsin_khan: And those who fear the torment of their Lord,
27.arberry: and go in fear of the chastisement of their Lord

28.sahih_international: Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not that from which one is safe -
28.pickthall: Lo! the doom of their Lord is that before which none can feel secure -
28.yusuf_ali: For their Lord's displeasure is the opposite of Peace and Tranquillity;-
28.shakir: Surely the chastisement of their Lord is (a thing) not to be felt secure of--
28.muhammad_sarwar: the punishment of their Lord is not something for them to feel secure of,
28.mohsin_khan: Verily! The torment of their Lord is that before which none can feel secure,
28.arberry: (from their Lord's chastisement none feels secure)

29.sahih_international: And those who guard their private parts
29.pickthall: And those who preserve their chastity
29.yusuf_ali: And those who guard their chastity,
29.shakir: And those who guard their private parts,
29.mohsin_khan: And those who guard their chastity (i.e. private parts from illegal sexual acts).

30.sahih_international: Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they are not to be blamed -
30.pickthall: Save with their wives and those whom their right hands possess, for thus they are not blameworthy;
30.yusuf_ali: Except with their wives and the (captives) whom their right hands possess,- for (then) they are not to be blamed,
30.shakir: Except in the case of their wives or those whom their right hands possess-- for these surely are not to be blamed,
30.muhammad_sarwar: except from their wives and slave girls, in which case they are not to be blamed,
30.mohsin_khan: Except with their wives and the (women slaves and captives) whom their right hands possess, for (then) they are not to be blamed,
30.arberry: save from their wives and what their right hands own, then not being blameworthy

31.sahih_international: But whoever seeks beyond that, then they are the transgressors -
31.pickthall: But whoso seeketh more than that, those are they who are transgressors;
31.yusuf_ali: But those who trespass beyond this are transgressors;-
31.shakir: But he who seeks to go beyond this, these it is that go beyond the limits--
31.muhammad_sarwar: but whoever goes beyond this is a transgressor;
31.mohsin_khan: But whosoever seeks beyond that, then it is those who are trespassers.
31.arberry: (but whoso seeks after more than that, they are the transgressors),

32.sahih_international: And those who are to their trusts and promises attentive
32.pickthall: And those who keep their pledges and their covenant,
32.yusuf_ali: And those who respect their trusts and covenants;
32.shakir: And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenant
32.muhammad_sarwar: who honor their trust and promises,
32.mohsin_khan: And those who keep their trusts and covenants;
32.arberry: and who preserve their trusts and their covenant,

33.sahih_international: And those who are in their testimonies upright
33.pickthall: And those who stand by their testimony
33.yusuf_ali: And those who stand firm in their testimonies;
33.shakir: And those who are upright in their testimonies,
33.muhammad_sarwar: who testify to what they have witnessed,
33.mohsin_khan: And those who stand firm in their testimonies;

34.sahih_international: And those who [carefully] maintain their prayer:
34.pickthall: And those who are attentive at their worship.
34.yusuf_ali: And those who guard (the sacredness) of their worship;-
34.shakir: And those who keep a guard on their prayer,
34.muhammad_sarwar: and (finally) those who do not miss their ritual - prayers at the prescribed times;
34.mohsin_khan: And those who guard their Salat (prayers) well.

35.sahih_international: They will be in gardens, honored.
35.pickthall: These will dwell in Gardens, honoured.
35.yusuf_ali: Such will be the honoured ones in the Gardens (of Bliss).
35.shakir: Those shall be in gardens, honored.
35.muhammad_sarwar: such people will receive due honor in Paradise.
35.mohsin_khan: Such shall dwell in the Gardens (i.e. Paradise) honoured.
35.arberry: Those shall be in Gardens, high-honoured.

36.sahih_international: So what is [the matter] with those who disbelieve, hastening [from] before you, [O Muhammad],
36.pickthall: What aileth those who disbelieve, that they keep staring toward thee (O Muhammad), open-eyed,
36.yusuf_ali: Now what is the matter with the Unbelievers that they rush madly before thee-
36.shakir: But what is the matter with those who disbelieve that they hasten on around you,
36.muhammad_sarwar: What is wrong with the disbelievers who roam around you (Muhammad),
36.mohsin_khan: So what is the matter with those who disbelieve that they hasten to listen from you (O Muhammad SAW), in order to belie you and to mock at you, and at Allah's Book (this Quran).
36.arberry: What ails the unbelievers, running with outstretched necks

37.sahih_international: [To sit] on [your] right and [your] left in separate groups?
37.pickthall: On the right and on the left, in groups?
37.yusuf_ali: From the right and from the left, in crowds?
37.shakir: On the right hand and on the left, in sundry parties?
37.muhammad_sarwar: left and right, in numerous groups?
37.mohsin_khan: (Sitting) in groups on the right and on the left (of you, O Muhammad SAW)?
37.arberry: towards thee on the right hand and on the left hand in knots?

38.sahih_international: Does every person among them aspire to enter a garden of pleasure?
38.pickthall: Doth every man among them hope to enter the Garden of Delight?
38.yusuf_ali: Does every man of them long to enter the Garden of Bliss?
38.shakir: Does every man of them desire that he should be made to enter the garden of bliss?
38.muhammad_sarwar: Does every one of them desire to enter the bountiful Paradise?
38.mohsin_khan: Does every man of them hope to enter the Paradise of delight?
38.arberry: What, is every man of them eager to be admitted to a Garden of Bliss?

39.sahih_international: No! Indeed, We have created them from that which they know.
39.pickthall: Nay, verily. Lo! We created them from what they know.
39.yusuf_ali: By no means! For We have created them out of the (base matter) they know!
39.shakir: By no means! Surely We have created them of what they know.
39.muhammad_sarwar: By no means! For they know very well out of what We have created them (The human being's naturally growing from a living germ, without discipline and good deeds will not result in virtue).
39.mohsin_khan: No, that is not like that! Verily, We have created them out of that which they know!
39.arberry: Not so; for We have created them of what they know.

40.sahih_international: So I swear by the Lord of [all] risings and settings that indeed We are able
40.pickthall: But nay! I swear by the Lord of the rising-places and the setting-places of the planets that We verily are Able
40.yusuf_ali: Now I do call to witness the Lord of all points in the East and the West that We can certainly-
40.shakir: But nay! I swear by the Lord of the Easts and the Wests that We are certainly able
40.muhammad_sarwar: I do not need to swear by the Lord of the eastern and western regions that We have certainly all the power
40.mohsin_khan: So I swear by the Lord of all [the three hundred and sixty (360)] points of sunrise and sunset in the east and the west that surely We are Able
40.arberry: No! I swear by the Lord of the Easts and Wests, surely We are able

41.sahih_international: To replace them with better than them; and We are not to be outdone.
41.pickthall: To replace them by (others) better than them. And we are not to be outrun.
41.yusuf_ali: Substitute for them better (men) than they; And We are not to be defeated (in Our Plan).
41.shakir: To bring instead (others) better than them, and We shall not be overcome.
41.muhammad_sarwar: to replace them by a better people and none can challenge Our power.
41.mohsin_khan: To replace them by (others) better than them; and We are not to be outrun.
41.arberry: to substitute a better than they; We shall not be outstripped.

42.sahih_international: So leave them to converse vainly and amuse themselves until they meet their Day which they are promised -
42.pickthall: So let them chat and play until they meet their Day which they are promised,
42.yusuf_ali: So leave them to plunge in vain talk and play about, until they encounter that Day of theirs which they have been promised!-
42.shakir: Therefore leave them alone to go on with the false discourses and to sport until they come face to face with that day of theirs with which they are threatened;
42.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), leave them alone to dispute and play until they face the Day with which they have been threatened:
42.mohsin_khan: So leave them to plunge in vain talk and play about, until they meet their Day which they are promised.
42.arberry: Then leave them alone to plunge and play until they encounter that day of theirs which they are promised,

43.sahih_international: The Day they will emerge from the graves rapidly as if they were, toward an erected idol, hastening.
43.pickthall: The day when they come forth from the graves in haste, as racing to a goal,
43.yusuf_ali: The Day whereon they will issue from their sepulchres in sudden haste as if they were rushing to a goal-post (fixed for them),-
43.shakir: The day on which they shall come forth from their graves in haste, as if they were hastening on to a goal,
43.muhammad_sarwar: the Day when they rush out of their graves as if racing towards a signpost,
43.mohsin_khan: The Day when they will come out of the graves quickly as racing to a goal,
43.arberry: the day they shall come forth from the tombs hastily, as if they were hurrying unto a waymark,

44.sahih_international: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. That is the Day which they had been promised.
44.pickthall: With eyes aghast, abasement stupefying them: Such is the Day which they are promised.
44.yusuf_ali: Their eyes lowered in dejection,- ignominy covering them (all over)! such is the Day the which they are promised!
44.shakir: Their eyes cast down; disgrace shall overtake them; that is the day which they were threatened with.
44.muhammad_sarwar: with their eyes cast down and covered by disgrace; the day about which they were promised.
44.mohsin_khan: With their eyes lowered in fear and humility, ignominy covering them (all over)! That is the Day which they were promised!
44.arberry: humbled their eyes, overspreading them abasement. That is the day which they were promised.
